title: The 5 Tallest Ferris Wheels on Earth, Ranked (No London Eye)

scenes.text: The five tallest Ferris wheels on Earth. The London Eye doesn't make the list.

scenes.label: Bailang River · 145 m
scenes.text: Number five: the Bailang River wheel in China. 145 meters, built into a bridge, with no spokes at all.

scenes.label: Star of Nanchang · 160 m
scenes.text: Number four: the Star of Nanchang, also in China. 160 meters, and the world's tallest when it opened in 2006.

scenes.label: Singapore Flyer · 165 m
scenes.text: Number three: the Singapore Flyer. 165 meters, with 28 capsules that each carry 28 people.

scenes.label: High Roller · 167.6 m
scenes.text: Number two: the High Roller in Las Vegas. 167.6 meters, ahead of Singapore by less than three.

scenes.label: Ain Dubai · 250 m
scenes.text: Number one: Ain Dubai. 250 meters, nearly twice the height of the London Eye, with room for 1,750 riders.

description:
The five tallest Ferris wheels ever opened to the public, ranked by height.
Ain Dubai on Bluewaters Island is the tallest at 250 metres and can carry 1,750 people. It is followed by the High Roller in Las Vegas (167.6 m, opened 2014), the Singapore Flyer (165 m, 2008), the Star of Nanchang in China (160 m, 2006) and the spokeless Bailang River Bridge Ferris Wheel in Weifang, China (145 m, 2017). The Sun of Moscow (140 m) and the London Eye (135 m) miss the list.
Which one would you ride first?
first_comment: The London Eye is only seventh, at 135 meters. Which would you ride first, and what should we rank next?
